text:
Olivia R: Quick follow-up on the AuthN/AuthZ RFC — I sketched an API key scoping model that distinguishes org-wide keys, project keys, and service tokens. Need input on: permission granularity (role vs. permission list), key rotation UX, and service->service auth pattern (mTLS vs signed JWT). TL;DR: I'm leaning toward role-based tokens with allow-lists per project and short TTLs for service tokens. Thoughts?

Matt H: +1 to short TTLs for service tokens. We should avoid org-wide keys for critical ops. How do we plan to handle cross-project read-only use cases?

Sridhar: for cross-project reads, propose a 'delegated role' where a project can grant 'read' permission to another project principal. Implementation: policy service stores mapping. Caveat: audit complexity and potential explosion of transient grants.

Olivia R: Agreed. Concerned about explosion of role variants. Maybe canonical roles (owner/editor/viewer) + permission overrides per resource. That keeps UI simpler and maps well to RBAC checks in runtime.

Ida: rotation UX — I'd prefer automatic key rotation for service tokens with a 1hr overlap window and a visible rotation timeline in Console. For API keys used by humans, manual rotate with pre-rotation warning and single-click revoke.

Owen: mTLS is great for zero-trust but ops-heavy for customers. Signed JWTs (short-lived, e.g. 5m) + KMS-backed signing for our managed services and a signer sidecar for private deployments seems simpler. We can support mTLS as enterprise opt-in.

DeployBot: Notice: deployment mysvc/1.4 created new service principal svc-mysvc-prod

Sridhar: Also: add rate-limiting on privileged tokens, and require explicit owner approval + 2FA for org-level key creation. For delegated roles, include a TTL and audit entry for each grant.

Olivia R: +1 on approvals. Plan update (working list):
- Canonical RBAC roles: owner/editor/viewer
- Permission overrides per resource for fine-grained cases
- Delegated roles for cross-project read w/ TTL and audit entries
- Service tokens: default = signed short-lived JWTs (rotation automated)
- mTLS = optional enterprise add-on
- Rotation UX: automatic for service tokens (with overlap) + manual for user keys
- Org-level keys require owner approval and audit log
I'll update the RFC and add a migration plan + audit log schema.

Matt H: Please add sample policy snippets and a token introspection endpoint. Example snippet for policy catalog: 
```
resource "inference:model" "read" {
  role = "viewer"
  principals = ["project:analytics"]
}
```
Also note how policy evaluation happens in the runtime (cached decisions vs live introspection).

Olivia R: Good call. I'll include both approaches: cached policy decisions with short TTL and a fallback introspection endpoint for admin workflows.

Olivia R: Thanks all. @Ida can you draft rotation UX mocks? @Owen can you outline the JWT signing/KMS flow and signer-sidecar approach for Private?

Ida: On it. ETA EOD tomorrow.

Owen: I'll write an initial KMS + signer sequence doc by Monday and include sequence diagrams for hosted vs private.

Olivia R: Perfect — once we have those I'll push RFC update and schedule a quick sync (15m) to close design decisions. :thumbsup:
